definitions: A provision in the treaties of the European Union that allows for a change from a specific decision-making procedure to a more general one, typically from unanimity to qualified majority voting, without a formal treaty amendment.
A mechanism within EU law enabling the European Council or Council of Ministers to alter voting procedures for certain policy areas.
examples: The passerelle clause was invoked to streamline decision-making.
Debate centered on the application of the passerelle clause.
Member states discussed the implications of using the passerelle clause.
